text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert group fired: inference-queue-delay (service=inference-service). Multiple regions (us-west1, eu-central) showing >500ms queue latency. Paging primary on-call now.
maya patel: saw the pages, thanks bot. are these coming in bursts or steady?
aj chen: they landed in bursts for me, ~10 pages in 2m, then quiet, then more. paging storm? :man_facepalming:
devon park: looking at PD — seems like dedupe didn't group because alerts have slightly different annotations (region tag vs zone).
pd-bot: PagerDuty: Incident 009867 created for inference-service. Acknowledgment pending.
aj chen: acked on PD. I see 21 alerts across 3 hosts. I already muted phone, will triage on slack.
maya patel: thanks. if it's a real degradation we should follow incident playbook, otherwise we silence and fix grouping rules.
devon park: quick check: redis-backed queue is healthy, CPU fine. KPIs show a spike in tail latencies correlating with a batch job that started at 02:12 UTC.
incident-bot: auto-grouping status: grouping key = alertname + service + region. Matching fuzzy? false.
aj chen: devon, can you confirm batch job ID? If that's root cause, we can throttle it or roll it back.
devon park: batch job id job-2026-03-14-0212. It's a high-concurrency eval run that we shouldn't have scheduled during peak - ops error. I've asked scheduler to stop it.
ops-bot: Scheduler: cancelled job job-2026-03-14-0212 (requested by devon park).
maya patel: ok that should reduce new alerts. but we still have a paging storm in PD. recommending temporary silence for the noisy alerts and then restore once burst subsides.
aj chen: agree. I'll create a PagerDuty silence for inference-service for 30m and note we need dedupe rule follow-up.
pd-bot: Command suggestion: ``pdsilence create --service inference-service --duration 30m --reason "paging storm after cancelled batch"``
aj chen: running that now.
aj chen: pd: silence created (30m) by aj chen — ID s-72c4. Adding note to incident: "temporary suppression while we confirm root cause; do not auto-escalate"
incident-bot: Update: silence s-72c4 applied, will suppress new low-priority pages for 1800s.
maya patel: good. two action items: 1) fix dedupe fingerprint to ignore zone-level noise and prefer region-level; 2) add scheduler window guard for heavy evals. I'll file a postmortem for the follow-up.
devon park: working on alert manager rule patch now. Proposed fingerprint change: ``fingerprint: hash(alertname + service + coalesce(region, substring(zone,0,3)))``. Will send PR in eng-infra.
aj chen: also updating PD escalation rule: if >5 distinct hosts in 3m, still page — that keeps us safe if this was multi-host production issue.
incident-bot: Note: auto-grouping heuristics temporarily disabled for inference-service during ongoing suppression to prevent double-suppressing.
samira khan: I'm on standby; taking handoff at 03:00 UTC. if anything pops after aj signs off, @samira will own.
aj chen: copying timeline into incident ticket and handing off to samira at 03:00. I'll remove myself from PD on-call after 03:05.
maya patel: can we add a tiny SRR (silence + reason) in the incident log so on-call rotation knows why pages were suppressed?
aj chen: added note: "Silenced for 30m due to scheduler-induced paging storm; root cause cancelled; follow-ups assigned to eng-infra and scheduler teams."
incident-bot: housekeeping: grouped 21 alerts into 3 incidents before suppression, 0 new pages forwarded to on-call during silence.
devon park: PR open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eng-infra/pull/431 — dedupe rule + unit tests. Please review.
maya patel: thanks team. leaving this thread for postmortem. tagging @oncall-rotation to capture in weekly rota notes. :white_check_mark:
oncall-rotation: Recorded incident in rotation log: 2026-03-14 02:12 UTC - inference paging storm - silence applied - follow-ups assigned to eng-infra (dedupe) & scheduler (guardrails).
samira khan: took over PD at 03:00; verified no new pages. will keep monitoring for 1h then close ticket if stable.
aj chen: handoff done, signing off. :wave:
maya patel: postmortem owner: maya patel. ETA for draft: EOD today.
incident-bot: Incident closed by automation at 04:05 UTC (no new alerts after suppression and scheduler rollback). Summary: paging storm caused by locationally-variant alert labels + a high-concurrency eval job; mitigations: scheduler cancel, PD silence, dedupe rule PR, escalation tuning.
maya patel: great, will link this thread in the PM. Thanks all. :tada:
